Name: ColumnPadStudio Program Map
Description: A high-level workflow map of how ColumnPadStudio is organised, how the main features connect, and what must stay clean when the app is changed.

Nodes.Title: Start app
Nodes.Description: The app launches into the WPF shell and restores usable state before the user starts writing.
Nodes.Goal: Open ColumnPadStudio with the right theme, preferences, recovery state, and default workspace.
Nodes.Instructions: Start in App.xaml/App.xaml.cs and MainWindow.xaml/MainWindow.xaml.cs. Keep startup light, keep crash handling clear, and avoid hiding feature wiring in unrelated files.
Nodes.ExpectedOutput: A stable main window with one active workspace and a ready editor surface.

ChecklistItems.Text: Load app resources and theme dictionaries without missing resource errors.
Restore preferences before the user sees the main editor.
Offer recovery only when a real recovery snapshot exists.

Nodes.Title: Workspace shell
Nodes.Description: Workspace tabs hold separate MainViewModel instances and control what the main window is editing.
Nodes.Goal: Keep workspace creation, rename, delete, scroll buttons, active state, and save-before-close behaviour consistent.
Nodes.Instructions: Use MainWindow.Workspaces.cs, WorkspaceSession.cs, MainWindow.WorkspaceSessions.cs, MainWindow.SaveBeforeExit.cs, and WorkspaceLifecycleService.cs as the single workspace path.
Nodes.ExpectedOutput: Multiple workspaces behave like separate documents without clashing with column actions.

ChecklistItems.Text: Workspace right-click actions affect only the workspace tab.
Workspace overflow uses tab scroll controls only when needed.
Multi-workspace save creates a workspace-session file, not a fake single layout.

Nodes.Title: Editor view model
Nodes.Description: MainViewModel owns the editable layout state: columns, global editor settings, file state, and layout JSON.
Nodes.Goal: Keep the app state readable and split by responsibility instead of rebuilding one huge view model file.
Nodes.Instructions: Use MainViewModel.cs plus the partial files for columns, fonts, file state, persistence, schema, migration, and JSON helpers. New state should live in the matching partial file.
Nodes.ExpectedOutput: Column count, selected column, font settings, proofing language, theme, save state, and status text all update from one reliable source.

ChecklistItems.Text: Do not duplicate save/load state outside MainViewModel file-state and persistence partials.
Keep migration code separate from normal save code.
New layout fields must round-trip through the layout schema.

Nodes.Title: Column editor control
Nodes.Description: ColumnEditorControl is the repeated editor surface for each column, including text editing, gutters, context menus, paste behaviour, spell check, and image UI.
Nodes.Goal: Keep every column visually and behaviourally consistent, including columns added later.
Nodes.Instructions: Use ColumnEditorControl.xaml and the partial files for lifecycle, menus, gutter, paste, and interactions. Fix column behaviour here when it belongs to every column.
Nodes.ExpectedOutput: All columns share the same resize behaviour, line-number gutter, context menu style, proofing behaviour, and attachment controls.

ChecklistItems.Text: Context menus should not duplicate main menu defaults.
Spell-check suggestions should appear where the spelling error is clicked.
Line number and checklist metadata should stay aligned after paste, load, and scroll.

Nodes.Title: Choose file route
Nodes.Description: Opening or saving must decide whether the user is working with raw text, a concise JSON export, layout JSON, workspace-session JSON, or a workflow.
Nodes.Goal: Send each file format through the right path without overwriting source files unexpectedly.
Nodes.Instructions: Use FileWorkflowService, WorkspaceImportRules, MainWindow.FileSession.cs, MainViewModel.FileState.cs, and MainViewModel.Persistence.cs. Keep app-native files separate from human-readable exports.
Nodes.ExpectedOutput: The app knows whether to load plain text, import an export, restore a layout, or restore multiple workspaces.

ChecklistItems.Text: Plain .txt files must not be auto-split unless they contain ColumnPad export markers.
Source text files and concise JSON exports require Save As before overwrite.
.columnpad.json remains the full app layout format.

Nodes.Title: Layout and session storage
Nodes.Description: The app saves one workspace as layout JSON and multiple workspaces as a workspace-session JSON.
Nodes.Goal: Preserve text, column widths, line modes, checklist metadata, images, theme, language, and file references cleanly.
Nodes.Instructions: Use MainViewModel.Persistence.cs, MainViewModel.LayoutSchema.cs, WorkspaceSessionFileService.cs, WorkspaceRecoveryStore.cs, and AtomicFileWriter.cs. Use atomic writes for anything saved to disk.
Nodes.ExpectedOutput: Saved files can be loaded again without losing layout or confusing external readers.

ChecklistItems.Text: Save JSON as real nested JSON, not escaped JSON strings.
Recovery snapshots should restore only valid layout data.
Text and JSON exports stay human-readable and marked.

Nodes.Title: Image attachments
Nodes.Description: Images are attached to columns and saved as part of the native layout format.
Nodes.Goal: Let users add and resize pictures without pretending pictures are plain text.
Nodes.Instructions: Use MainWindow.Images.cs, ColumnImageFileService.cs, ColumnImageViewModel.cs, ColumnEditorControl.xaml, and layout persistence. Keep image storage linked to native layout JSON.
Nodes.ExpectedOutput: Images appear inside the right column, can be resized, and round-trip with app layout files.

ChecklistItems.Text: Auto-grow the column only when the image needs more width.
Remove image files safely when attachments are deleted.
Do not place image data inside plain .txt or concise JSON exports.

Nodes.Title: Proofing and settings
Nodes.Description: The toolbar and menus control editor font, theme, spell check, language, line paper, wrap, and line numbers.
Nodes.Goal: Keep settings in one visible, consistent place and avoid duplicated settings in right-click menus.
Nodes.Instructions: Use MainWindow.xaml, MainWindow.ViewModes.cs, MainViewModel.Fonts.cs, AppPreferencesService.cs, ThemePresetService.cs, ThemeResourceService.cs, and resources under Resources.
Nodes.ExpectedOutput: Settings apply to all relevant columns and persist cleanly without a bolted-on toolbar feel.

ChecklistItems.Text: Toolbar highlights and spacing should match normal app controls.
Spell check language follows the selected proofing language when Windows dictionaries exist.
Dark and light modes should use the same control structure with different resources.

Nodes.Title: Workflow builder
Nodes.Description: The workflow builder lets users create reusable process maps with starters, nodes, links, JSON import/export, and human-readable TXT/MD exports.
Nodes.Goal: Make workflows useful as app data and readable outside the app.
Nodes.Instructions: Use WorkflowBuilderWindow.xaml/.cs, WorkflowBuilderViewModel partials, WorkflowService.cs, WorkflowDefinition.cs, node/link/checklist models, and WorkflowTemplateCatalog.cs.
Nodes.ExpectedOutput: Users can create, save, import, export, and read workflows without confusing JSON data with plain documentation.

ChecklistItems.Text: Keep .workflow.json as the editable/importable workflow format.
Keep TXT and MD exports human-readable and one-way.
Workflow nodes should include goal, instructions, expected output, and checklist data.

Nodes.Title: Domain rules
Nodes.Description: Small domain helpers keep list markers, checklist metrics, paste presets, workspace constraints, and import detection out of UI code.
Nodes.Goal: Keep reusable rules testable and independent from WPF controls.
Nodes.Instructions: Use ColumnPadStudio.Domain for list and workspace rules. Put logic here when it does not need WPF objects or window state.
Nodes.ExpectedOutput: Paste, checklist, import detection, and constraint rules can be tested without launching the app.

ChecklistItems.Text: Do not copy parser logic into controls.
Keep marker parsing and import rules covered by domain tests.
Only UI-specific code should stay in the WPF project.

Nodes.Title: Quality checks
Nodes.Description: Build, domain tests, smoke tests, and UI sanity checks protect the app after cleanup or feature work.
Nodes.Goal: Catch broken wiring before upload or release.
Nodes.Instructions: Use tests/ColumnPadStudio.Domain.Tests and tests/ColumnPadStudio.SmokeTests. Run release build and targeted app checks before publishing.
Nodes.ExpectedOutput: The app builds, core behaviour passes tests, and obvious UI wiring still works.

ChecklistItems.Text: Run release build with NuGet audit disabled only when needed for local SDK noise.
Run domain tests for pure logic changes.
Run smoke tests for WPF wiring, persistence, workflow, and UI resource checks.

Nodes.Title: Release package
Nodes.Description: Publishing creates the single EXE release asset and updates documentation so the GitHub page looks like a real app.
Nodes.Goal: Ship only needed files, release notes, README updates, and a clean one-EXE build.
Nodes.Instructions: Use README.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/releases, RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md, the publish profile, and GitHub release assets. Keep repo cleanup separate from app feature changes.
Nodes.ExpectedOutput: GitHub shows a clear app page, current release notes, and a downloadable single EXE.

ChecklistItems.Text: Update README and screenshot when UI meaningfully changes.
Do not upload build junk, temporary files, or local recovery data.
Attach the current single EXE to the release.

Nodes.Title: Healthy app
Nodes.Description: The app remains understandable, useful, and ready for future work.
Nodes.Goal: Keep ColumnPadStudio professional without redesigning it into a different product.
Nodes.Instructions: When changing the app, follow this map: preserve useful features, remove dead or duplicated systems, and rebuild only the areas that are safer to rebuild than patch.
Nodes.ExpectedOutput: A clean multi-column writing app with reliable workspaces, save/load, proofing, image attachments, workflow tools, and release process.

ChecklistItems.Text: No fake screens or dead systems remain connected.
No feature has two competing sources of truth.
Another developer can follow the structure without guessing.
